title: Storage Terraform module for Private: hardening, snapshot lifecycle, and health checks
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reusable, hardened Terraform module to provision storage primitives for Private (VPC) deployments: EBS volumes, EFS filesystems, and S3 buckets. The module must enforce encryption-by-default (KMS-managed or customer-specified CMKs), offer snapshot/backup lifecycle controls, provide sane tagging for chargeback and auditing, and export health-checking metrics and alerts for on-call automation. This ticket covers the design, implementation, documentation, and a rollout plan that keeps backward compatibility for existing stacks.
implementation_plan: 1) Define module inputs/outputs and defaults: encryption_mode (aws:kms|AES256), kms_key_arn, enable_snapshots (bool), snapshot_retention_days (int), lifecycle_rules (for S3), efs_performance_mode, ebs_volume_types, tags map (default org/project/environment). 2) Enforce governance: validate inputs with precondition checks, deny public ACLs for S3, block unencrypted EBS/EFS creation. 3) Snapshot management: for EBS use AWS Data Lifecycle Manager or native snapshot resource with retention policy; for EFS integrate with backup plan (Backup vault) or scheduled Lambda; for S3 implement lifecycle rules and periodic cross-region replication for protected buckets. 4) Health checks: export CloudWatch metrics and alarms (snapshot-failure, backup-age, no-recent-snapshot), optional Lambda remediation to trigger ad-hoc snapshots and open incident if remediation fails. 5) IAM: module creates minimal service role for snapshot scheduling and optionally a cross-account KMS grants pattern. 6) CI/CD: add acceptance tests to terraform-qa pipeline using LocalStack and a small real-account test harness for KMS/EBS semantics. 7) Docs: usage examples, migration recipes for existing unencrypted resources, and upgrade notes for provider versions.
acceptance_criteria: - Module creates EBS/EFS/S3 resources with encryption enabled by default and accepts customer-supplied CMKs. - Snapshot lifecycle policy applied and retention verified via CloudWatch metrics. - Alarms trigger on backup failures in a test window and optional Lambda remediation runs. - Terraform plan detects non-specified kms_key_arn and applies default KMS key module output. - No S3 bucket is created with public ACL or public access block disabled by default. - Upgrade path documented and tested for at least 2 existing private deploy stacks.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Existing unencrypted resources could be disrupted during migration. Mitigation: provide a non-intrusive migration recipe: perform snapshot, create encrypted copy, failover during maintenance window, rollback steps. Risk: KMS key policy mistakes can break backups. Mitigation: standardize generated CMK policy template and include explicit terraform state warnings and a dry-run mode. Risk: Terraform provider changes (AWS provider v4->v5) affecting snapshot resources. Mitigation: pin provider versions in module and provide upgrade notes and CI matrix.
implementation_notes: - Start with EBS snapshot scheduler and KMS integration; EFS backup integration will follow in a second patch to keep changes small. - Use terraform modules/ submodules for each provider resource to keep drift reasoning simple. - Add feature flag 'enable_automatic_remediation' default false until oncall runbooks updated.
documentation_tasks: - Write README with inputs/outputs and example usage for VPC-private stacks. - Add migration doc for converting unencrypted EBS/S3 to encrypted with minimal downtime. - Publish example terragrunt wrapper for customer templates.
